label: <DEL> delimiter step in long sequences (L >= 6), scaled by length
explanation: Fires essentially only at the <DEL> delimiter step (recall_idx 0) and only when the sequence is long. It is silent for L = 3..5, weak and on about half of delimiters at L = 6, and on nearly every delimiter for L = 7..9. Magnitude rises with L: mass share goes 0.014 (L=6), 0.20 (L=7), 0.36 (L=8), 0.42 (L=9), and the top activations are all L = 8-9 delimiters. Token identity (out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, n_digits) has little effect. It never fires in the copy phase. In the original phase it fires only weakly, on about 0.1% of the last original token at L = 9. The narrower (phase==1)&(L>=7) has precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.986 but misses the weak L=6 firings.

issues: Every factual claim checks out on dev and test. All activation mass is on the delimiter step. There are 0 copy-phase activations. The original phase has 941 activations, all at L = 9 with to_go = 0, and together they carry 0.0001 of the mass. Nothing fires for L <= 5. About 54% of L = 6 delimiters fire (dev precision 0.538), carrying 0.014 of the mass. Almost every L >= 7 delimiter fires: the predicate (phase==1)&(L>=7) has precision 1.0 (test recall 0.847, mass recall 0.986). The mass shares by L are 0.20, 0.36 and 0.42 for L = 7, 8 and 9 with roughly equal active counts, so magnitude does grow with L.

Test score of (phase==1)&(L>=6) reproduces: precision 0.884, recall 0.997, F1 0.937, mass recall 1.000. The misses (888 test steps, 0.0% of mass) are all the weak last-original-token firings at L = 9, which is scattered noise.

The false positives are systematic but low-mass: all 38,670 test false positives are L = 6 delimiters that stay silent. Which L = 6 delimiters fire depends partly on which tokens appear in the sequence. Firing rate given that a token appears ranges from 0.40 (digit 0) to 0.71 ('r'), and the effect is spread across many tokens rather than one. So the claim that token identity has 'almost no effect' is only true for L >= 7; at the L = 6 threshold, content shifts the decision.

A tuned refinement brings the L = 6 decision in: count tokens from a 'raises firing' set minus tokens from a 'lowers firing' set, with the sets chosen on dev. It raises test F1 from 0.937 to 0.955 (precision 0.952, recall 0.958). This is a modest gain on a part of the activation carrying about 1.4% of the mass. It does not change the label, so the explanation stands, with a caveat about content dependence at L = 6.
